content:
Data handling in Class 4 reads pictographs with keys, bar graphs and tables — careful-counting marks that add up fast. Here is what the IMO Class 4 data handling chapter tests, the facts, the slips, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Data Handling chapter tests

  • Pictographs with keys/scales (including half-symbols)
  • Bar graphs and their scales
  • Tally marks and tables
  • Interpretation — most/fewest, how many more, totals

Key facts your child should know

  • Multiply symbols × key; a half-symbol is half the key.
  • Read each bar against the scale, not by eye.
  • Tallies count in fives — the fifth mark crosses the four.
  • "How many more" → subtract; total → add every row.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring the key and counting symbols as 1.
  • Misreading a bar that ends between grid lines.
  • Adding rows when the question asks for a difference.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Data Handling Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 4: Data Handling

questions.q: A table records visitors to a science exhibition over five days: Wed 70, Thu 65, Fri 85, Sat 110, Sun 95. What is the total for all five days?
A pie chart shows the favourite fruits of some students, 200 students in all. One quarter of the pie shows those who chose mango. How many students is that?
The pencils bought by some children were: 4, 6, 6, 8, 6, 10, 4. What is the mode of this data?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 6 appears 3 times — more than any other value.

questions.q: A bar graph uses the scale 1 unit = 5. How many units tall should the bar for children who chose football be, if the value is 45?
questions.explanation: Height in units = value ÷ scale = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 units.

questions.q: A table shows rainfall over four weeks: Week 1 35, Week 2 50, Week 3 20, Week 4 45. What is the total rainfall in mm?
A monitor makes a tally chart of 37 ducklings counted at a village pond, marking bundles of five. How many complete bundles of five will the tally have?
questions.explanation: 37 = 7 × 5 + 2, so there are 7 complete bundles and 2 single marks left over.

questions.q: A bar graph uses the scale 1 unit = 20. How many units tall should the bar for trees planted by Class 4 be, if the value is 140?
questions.explanation: Height in units = value ÷ scale = 140 ÷ 20 = 7 units.

questions.q: On a bar graph the scale is 1 unit = 10. The bar showing mangoes picked on Tuesday is 9 units tall. What value does the bar show?
Here are the fruits picked on chits in a class game, in order: guava, litchi, guava, papaya, guava, litchi, cherry. Which one is the mode of this data?
questions.explanation: The mode is the item that occurs most often. "guava" occurs 3 times, more than any other.

questions.q: A graph shows mango trees in four orchards: Orchard K 58, Orchard L 72, Orchard M 66, Orchard N 49. Which one is the second highest?
questions.explanation: From highest to lowest: Orchard L 72, Orchard M 66, Orchard K 58, Orchard N 49. The second highest is Orchard M (66).

faq.q: What does a half-symbol mean in a pictograph?
faq.a: Half the key. If one symbol = 10 books, a half-symbol = 5 books.

faq.q: How do you read a bar graph scale?
faq.a: Check what each grid line stands for (1, 2, 5, 10 …) and read the bar top against it.
